name: Nethanel
overview: Nethanel was a male leader from the tribe of Issachar during the time of the Exodus. He served as the head of his tribe at the time of the census, indicating a position of responsibility and leadership among the Israelites. His role is specifically noted during the numbering of the people, reflecting his importance in the tribal structure.
namesAndTitles: The name Nethanel means "G-d has given," highlighting a recognition of divine provision or blessing. This proper name, recorded in Numbers 1:8, reflects the spiritual understanding of his identity within the community.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Nethanel was the son of Zuar, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Nethanel's significance lies in his leadership role as head of the tribe of Issachar during the Exodus census. This position underscores his trusted status among the Israelites and his participation in the orderly organization of the people as they prepared for their journey. His mention in Numbers 1:8 situates him within the broader narrative of God's covenant people being counted and arranged under divine guidance.
